recommendedTextbook.title: Basic Science for Junior Secondary Schools 2
recommendedTextbook.author: F.O.C. Ndu, P. Asun, J.O. Aina
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Living Things: Habitats and Environmental Adaptations
subtopics: Definition of habitat (aquatic, terrestrial, arboreal)
Adaptive features of plants and animals to aquatic environments (mangrove swamps, fish gills)
Adaptive features to arid and savanna environments (cactus, camel)
objectives: Define habitat and categorize habitats into aquatic and terrestrial types
Describe specific morphological adaptations of tilapia fish to fresh and brackish water
Relate plant adaptations in Nigerian Guinea Savanna to water conservation

topics.topic: Human Respiratory System and Mechanism of Breathing
subtopics: Structure of the respiratory tract (trachea, bronchi, lungs, alveoli)
Inhalation and exhalation mechanics (role of diaphragm and intercostal muscles)
Differences between breathing and cellular respiration
objectives: Identify and label principal organs of the human respiratory system
Demonstrate rib cage and diaphragm movement using a bell-jar balloon model
Differentiate internal cellular respiration from external pulmonary ventilation

topics.topic: Human Circulatory System and Blood Composition
subtopics: Structure and function of the heart (atria, ventricles, valves)
Composition of blood (red cells, white cells, platelets, plasma)
ABO blood grouping system and genotype awareness (AA, AS, SS)
objectives: Trace double circulation pathway through systemic and pulmonary circuits
Explain functions of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets
Discuss importance of pre-marital genotype counseling in Nigerian society

topics.topic: Human Digestive System and Enzyme Action
subtopics: Alimentary canal organs (mouth, esophagus, stomach, duodenum, ileum)
Mechanical vs chemical digestion
Action of digestive enzymes (ptyalin, pepsin, trypsin, lipase)
objectives: Trace path of swallowed food from mouth to rectum
Demonstrate starch breakdown by salivary amylase in the laboratory
Identify sites of absorption of digested nutrients into the bloodstream

topics.topic: Human Excretory System: Kidney and Skin Mechanics
subtopics: Meaning of excretion and excretory organs in humans
Structure of the kidney and nephron filtration unit
Structure of the human skin and sweat production
objectives: Distinguish between excretion of metabolic waste and egestion of feces
Label longitudinal section of human kidney and trace urine passage to the bladder
Explain thermoregulatory role of sweat glands during hot Nigerian afternoons

topics.topic: Kinetic Theory of Matter: Molecular Movement in Solids, Liquids & Gases
subtopics: Postulates of the kinetic theory of matter
Arrangement and motion of particles in solids, liquids, and gases
Diffusion and Brownian motion demonstrations
objectives: State postulates of the kinetic molecular theory
Demonstrate diffusion using potassium permanganate crystals in water and perfume in classroom air
Explain thermal expansion of matter based on kinetic energy of particles

subtopics: Comprehensive diagnostic assessment on Weeks 1-6 systems and kinetic theory
Practical laboratory test and corrective feedback
objectives: Evaluate pupil mastery of circulatory, respiratory, digestive, and excretory systems
Provide tiered remediation for students struggling with physiological pathways

topics.topic: Boiling, Evaporation and Thermal Energy Changes
subtopics: Meaning and differences between boiling and evaporation
Factors affecting evaporation rate (temperature, surface area, humidity, wind)
Cooling effect of evaporation in traditional clay pots
objectives: Contrast boiling with evaporation in terms of temperature, surface location, and bubbles
Investigate factors affecting water evaporation rate in school courtyard
Explain how traditional Nigerian earthenware water pots keep drinking water chilled

topics.topic: Work, Energy and Power: Quantitative Calculations
subtopics: Scientific definition of work done: Work = Force × Distance (W = F × d)
Calculations of work done in Joules
Concept of power as rate of doing work: Power = Work / Time (P = W / t in Watts)
objectives: Define work and power with their statutory S.I. units (Joules and Watts)
Calculate work done lifting bags of cement or water containers against gravity
Solve numerical word problems calculating electric generator power output

topics.topic: Simple Machines: Levers, Pulleys, and Mechanical Advantage
subtopics: Types of simple machines (levers, pulleys, inclined planes, wheel and axle)
Classes of levers (1st, 2nd, 3rd class with everyday tools: bottle opener, scissors, wheelbarrow)
Mechanical Advantage (MA), Velocity Ratio (VR), and Efficiency
objectives: Classify common tools used in Nigerian households into 1st, 2nd, or 3rd class levers
Calculate Mechanical Advantage using formula MA = Load / Effort
Explain why machine efficiency can never exceed 100% due to friction

topics.topic: Crude Oil and Petrochemicals: Refining and Petroleum in Nigeria
subtopics: Origin and formation of crude oil in the Niger Delta basin
Fractional distillation of petroleum (fractions: petroleum gas, petrol, kerosene, diesel, bitumen)
Economic importance and environmental hazards of oil spillage and bunkering
objectives: Describe formation of petroleum over millions of years from marine sediments
List key petroleum fractions in order of boiling point ranges
Analyze environmental devastation of oil spills on aquatic ecosystems in the Niger Delta

topics.topic: Thermal Energy Transfer: Conduction, Convection and Radiation
subtopics: Conduction in metals vs thermal insulators (cooking utensils with wooden handles)
Convection currents in fluids, sea breezes, and domestic hot water systems
Radiation from the Sun and solar cookers
objectives: Compare conduction, convection, and radiation with practical laboratory demonstrations
Explain daytime sea breeze and night land breeze along the Lagos coastline
Design a simple solar water heater utilizing absorption of radiant thermal energy

subtopics: Review of physiological systems, kinetic theory, machines, and crude oil refining
Terminal examination and broadsheet entry
objectives: Demonstrate complete mastery of JSS 2 Basic Science Term 1 syllabus
